necessary-vs-sufficient.stimulus: Every employee who completes the safety course receives a badge. Dana did not complete the course, so Dana will not receive a badge.
necessary-vs-sufficient.reason: Completing the course is enough to get a badge. The argument treats it as required. Dana could have earned a badge another way.

causal.stimulus: Neighborhoods with more street lamps report fewer break-ins. So installing street lamps reduces break-ins.
causal.reason: The evidence says two things go together. The conclusion picks one cause. Wealthier neighborhoods could have both more lamps and fewer break-ins.

part-vs-whole.stimulus: The faculty committee reached a wise decision, so every member of the committee must be wise.
part-vs-whole.reason: A trait of the whole group is pushed onto each member. A committee can decide wisely because of how it worked together, or because of a few members, while others are not wise.

unproven-vs-proven-false.stimulus: No study has shown that this herbal tea improves sleep, so it does not improve sleep.
unproven-vs-proven-false.reason: No one has shown it works. That is not the same as someone showing it does not. All we know is that it has not been shown.

ad-hominem.stimulus: The mayor's report says the new tram line is cost-effective. But the mayor's brother builds trams, so the report can be ignored.
ad-hominem.reason: The author rejects the report by pointing at who is connected to it. The report's numbers are the thing to check.

sampling.stimulus: I polled ten people leaving a vegan restaurant and nine said they would give up meat. So most residents of this city would give up meat.
sampling.reason: The ten people were selected for exactly the trait being measured. They are a small, biased sample of a whole city.

circular-reasoning.stimulus: The new rule is fair because it treats everyone justly.
circular-reasoning.reason: Treating everyone justly is just fair said another way. The reason repeats the conclusion.

internal-contradiction.stimulus: The report says that every employee finished the training this year. It also says that three employees never finished the training this year.
internal-contradiction.reason: If every employee finished, none can have missed it. The two claims are about the same employees, the same training and the same year, so they cannot both be true.

equivocation.stimulus: Laws are made by legislators. Gravity is a law of nature. So gravity was made by legislators.
equivocation.reason: The word law means a rule passed by a legislature in the first sentence and a regularity of nature in the second.

inappropriate-appeal.stimulus: A famous actor says this brand of ladder is the sturdiest, so it is the sturdiest.
inappropriate-appeal.reason: The only reason given is who said it. A famous actor is not an expert on ladder strength.

sleight-of-hand.stimulus: The new curriculum raises test scores. So it will make students love learning.
sleight-of-hand.reason: Love learning is a new term in the conclusion. Higher test scores are not basically the same thing.

sleazy-sales-pitch.stimulus: Choose the Harbor Hotel: it has a pool and a rooftop bar, while the Maple Inn has no gym and a slow elevator.
sleazy-sales-pitch.reason: You hear the Harbor's strengths and the Maple's weaknesses. Nothing about the Harbor's drawbacks or the Maple's strengths.

universal-desires.stimulus: This investment will double your money in ten years, so everyone should invest in it.
universal-desires.reason: The argument assumes everyone wants this kind of return. Some people do not want the risk, or the investment, at all.

value-assumptions.stimulus: The company lets employees work from home, so it is a more admirable employer.
value-assumptions.reason: Admirable is a loaded word the evidence never defined. Letting people work from home is one fact, not a verdict.

secret-downsides.stimulus: We should replace the paper forms with an app, because the app is faster.
secret-downsides.reason: Only the benefit is named. Training time, people without the app, or the cost of building it could outweigh the speed.

matrix_drills.stimulus: Anyone who holds a pilot's license is allowed to fly a plane. Marta is allowed to fly a plane, so Marta holds a pilot's license.
matrix_drills.reason: The relationship is an if-then rule, not one thing making another happen. The author reads the rule backwards.

matrix_drills.stimulus: A poll of the four thousand subscribers of a luxury travel magazine found that 90% plan to renew their passports, so most adults plan to renew theirs.
matrix_drills.reason: The sample is large, so size is not the problem. The problem is how it was selected: subscribers of a travel magazine are far more likely to travel.

matrix_drills.stimulus: The study shows the drug is effective at lowering blood pressure. So the drug is safe.
matrix_drills.reason: Two different words, effective and safe, are treated as equivalent. No single word shifts its meaning.

matrix_drills.stimulus: The restaurant uses locally sourced produce, so it is a morally better restaurant.
matrix_drills.reason: The new term in the conclusion is an evaluative word: morally better. Name the loaded word and it is Value Assumptions.

matrix_drills.stimulus: The critic says the bridge is unsafe. But nobody has found a crack in it, so the critic is wrong.
matrix_drills.reason: What is attacked is the lack of evidence, not the critic as a person. No cracks found is not proof the bridge is safe.

matrix_drills.stimulus: The firm's total revenue grew this year, so each of its offices must have grown.
matrix_drills.reason: The move is from the whole to each part, not from a sample to a population.

matrix_drills.stimulus: Switch to Brand A: it is cheaper and lasts longer, unlike Brand B, which is expensive and breaks easily.
matrix_drills.reason: Two options are compared, and only one side's strengths and the other side's weaknesses are given.

matrix_drills.stimulus: The city built more bike lanes this year. So the city has become more environmentally conscious.
matrix_drills.reason: The conclusion brings in a new term, environmentally conscious. It does not claim that one thing caused another.

matrix_drills.stimulus: Anything light is easy to carry. This shirt is light blue, so this shirt is easy to carry.
matrix_drills.reason: The rule is applied in the right direction: light, so easy to carry. But light means low weight in the rule and pale in the fact. One word, two senses.

matrix_drills.stimulus: The new phone plan saves money, so everyone should switch to it.
matrix_drills.reason: The unjustified claim is about what people want: it assumes everyone wants to save money in this way.
